title: The Tricycle, the Ice Pops and the School Shop That Became Wahaha
conflicts: First-year earnings: Zong (Wharton 2005) said 100,000 yuan; The World of Chinese says 220,000 yuan profit; Yicai gives 222,000 yuan net profit by May 1988. The story uses Zong's figure, attributed. Start-up money: 140,000 yuan borrowed (CNN, Yicai, World of Chinese) versus Fortune's '$22,000 family loan'; the story gives only the yuan sum and no lender. Drink 1988 (Yicai) versus factory 1989 (BBC, Wharton); both used for what each source dates. Cannery takeover 1990 (Zong) versus 1991 (BBC, Yicai, World of Chinese); 1991 used.
notes: Slate episode confirmed: a school-run sales department in Hangzhou's Shangcheng district, two retired teachers, ice pops, soft drinks and stationery sold to pupils, plus contract processing of tonics before the 1988 Wahaha drink. Funding marked bootstrapped (a loan and its own earnings, no outside investors until Danone in 1996), but the enterprise was collectively owned (Wharton says wholly state-owned until 2000), which the story states. CNN obituary cited via its KTVZ syndication because cnn.com did not load.
